The job prints a JSON run summary to stdout. That is the main operational output for cron logs.

## Optional Trigger Server

For initial testing you can run a small local HTTP trigger server. While it is running, it automatically polls Slack every 10 minutes by default using the same checkpoint fallback logic as the one-shot CLI. You can still kick off manual runs with `curl` when needed.

Start the server:

```bash
./.venv/bin/python -m slack_region_ingest.specials_job \
  serve \
  --region outer-banks \
  --config /absolute/path/to/regions.yml \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8787 \
  --trigger-token test-secret \
  --log-only
```

If you want the server process to perform real ingest automatically, omit `--log-only`.
If you want to disable the background poller and use HTTP triggers only, pass:

```bash
--poll-interval-seconds 0
```

Health check:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/healthz
```

Trigger a run:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/run \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Trigger-Token: test-secret' \
  -d '{"log_only": true}'
```

Optional request body fields:
- `dry_run`
- `log_only`
- `newsletter_only`
- `since`
- `skip_backend`

### Slack Slash Command

The trigger server also accepts Slack slash commands at:

```text
POST /slack/commands
```

Use this when you want newsletter generation to start from Slack instead of `curl`.

Requirements:
- add `signing_secret_env: SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET` (or `signing_secret`) in the region config
- update/reinstall the Slack app with the `commands` scope
- point the slash command request URL at your running trigger server, for example `https://your-server.example.com/slack/commands`

Behavior:
- the command works from any configured input channel, plus the configured `output_channel`
- it triggers a newsletter run for the region
- it skips backend upload
- it posts the resulting Google Doc link back into the Slack channel where the command was run

Example manifest settings are in [slack-app-manifest.yml](/Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/scrapers/slack_region_ingest/slack-app-manifest.yml).

### Local Socket Mode

For local development you can skip the public Slack request URL entirely and run the command listener over Socket Mode instead.

Requirements:
- enable Socket Mode on the Slack app
- create an app-level token with `connections:write`
- put it in `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`
- install the `websocket-client` dependency from `requirements.txt`

Run it like this:

```bash
./.venv/bin/python -m slack_region_ingest.specials_job \
  socket-serve \
  --region outer-banks \
  --config /absolute/path/to/regions.yml
```

Behavior:
- keeps the same 10-minute background poller by default
- receives `/newsletter` over Slack WebSocket delivery instead of HTTP using Slack SDK's `websocket-client` Socket Mode backend
- works from any configured input channel plus the configured `output_channel`
- triggers newsletter generation and skips backend upload

If you only want the Socket Mode command listener and no background polling:

```bash
./.venv/bin/python -m slack_region_ingest.specials_job \
  socket-serve \
  --region outer-banks \
  --config /absolute/path/to/regions.yml \
  --poll-interval-seconds 0
```

### Local Dual Listener

For the Slack-to-Discord overlap period, the recommended local workflow is the shared `listen` command. It starts one scheduled poll loop, then attaches Slack Socket Mode and the Discord gateway bot to the same runner/state store.

Run it like this:

```bash
./.venv/bin/python -m slack_region_ingest.specials_job \
  listen \
  --region outer-banks \
  --config /absolute/path/to/regions.yml
```

Behavior:
- starts Slack Socket Mode with the `websocket-client` backend when `slack.app_token` is configured
- starts the Discord gateway bot when `discord.bot_token` is configured
- keeps one shared run lock so scheduled polls and slash-command runs do not overlap
- adds Discord channel history backfill to the same ingest pass used by Slack

Discord setup for `listen`:
- install the bot with `bot` and `applications.commands`
- grant `View Channel`, `Read Message History`, and `Send Messages`
- enable the `MESSAGE_CONTENT` privileged intent for the bot application
- use a guild-scoped `/newsletter` command during local development for fast sync
- put the bot token in `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` (or inline `discord.bot_token`)

## Cron

Typical pattern is to keep the secrets in a small shell wrapper and let cron call that wrapper. Example wrapper:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/scrapers/slack_region_ingest
export SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=...
export EVENT_INGEST_SECRET=...

./.venv/bin/python -m slack_region_ingest.specials_job \
  run \
  --region outer-banks \
  --config /absolute/path/to/regions.yml
```

Example cron entry:

```cron
0 8 * * * /absolute/path/to/run_outer_banks_ingest.sh >> /var/log/slack-region-ingest.log 2>&1
```

## Tests

```bash
./.venv/bin/pytest tests -q
```

## Notes

- The runner keeps a SQLite checkpoint and per-branch retry state.
- `listen` is the recommended local command when Slack and Discord need to coexist.
- Beehiiv creation is grouped by pending run id.
- In `google_doc` mode the newsletter branch creates one Google Doc per region per day using `gog`.
- In `slack_file` mode the newsletter branch uploads Markdown and HTML files into Slack instead of calling Beehiiv.
- Backend upload retries package-by-package.
- The current analyzer is heuristic. The runner shape is ready for a stronger model-backed analyzer if you want to swap one in later.
- `THIS_WEEK`, `LATER`, `RECURRING`, and `IGNORE` are decided during analysis before Beehiiv/backend branching.

## Done — all 13 audit items, both repos

**web-backend (pushed to origin/main):**
- `170ac424` — items 1–4 + 10: weekday alignment service (`trips/services/recurrence_alignment.py`, corrects Sunday=0 payloads against description/title/start date, never rejects); exact-date matching for non-recurring near-dups and meal merges (kills F2 collapse); merge span clamp; `last_ingested_at` field + migration `0033`; 14-day recurrence horizon for scraped DAILY/WEEKLY; stale-zombie exclusion on specials page; per-event receipts in ingest response (`results`, `deactivated_event_ids` — aggregate counts unchanged).

**scrapers (local commits `08cdc1d`, `bbb590a`, `d991354`):**
- Items 6–7: `STRIP_RECURRENCE` gate mode demotes only offending items to single-day and publishes siblings (ends Hurricane Mo's-style blackouts); prompts state Monday=0 explicitly; `_reconcile_weekly_recurrence` fixes wrong-convention payloads pre-upload.
- Items 8–9: external_ids slug venue+date+meal instead of LLM title (attachment-group prefix preserved, replay-safe); multi-day flyers become one DAILY item with explicit end date (`recurrence_source="date_range"`, gate-exempt).
- Items 11–12: `specials_job reconcile` subcommand checks receipts vs public JSONL feed (missing/zombie/duplicate/weekday-mismatch findings, `--post-slack`); venue blocked 3 consecutive packages → one-time Slack alert, reset on success. New config: `backend.specials_feed_url`. README cron docs added.

**Tests:** backend — all new + touched suites pass (109 targeted + full `regions/` 123). Scraper — 178 pass. Pre-existing failures NOT from this work (verified on clean tree): `test_region_api_views` 2 failures, `test_trip_photos` OOM (web container 1GiB cap), scraper `test_weather` 1 failure.

**Remaining manual steps (prod, per your no-prod-commits flow):**
1. Pull on prod, `migrate` (adds `last_ingested_at`).
2. `python3 manage.py repair_region_event_ingest --source-key <obx-source-key>` — confirm zombies 153/339/738 + Sunday-convention rows listed, then re-run with `--apply`, then `audit_region_event_ingest` to confirm zeroed.
3. Deploy scraper to listener host; add `specials_feed_url` to `outer_banks.yml`; wire the reconcile cron.
4. After scraper deploy: one supervised `specials_job.py replay` over a recent window (`--log-only` first) to cut over external_ids; inspect `deactivated_event_ids` in receipts.

One caveat: backend commits used `SKIP=django-check-migrations` — the hook failure came from another agent's in-flight `events` work (their unstaged `models.py` + untracked migration confuse the stash-based check); your trips/regions migration state checks clean with the full tree.

Scraped payloads sometimes carry ``recurrence_days`` in the wrong weekday
convention (e.g. Sunday=0 instead of Python's Monday=0) or a ``start_date``
that contradicts the weekday named in the title. Alignment corrects the

Evidence precedence for WEEKLY items:
1. "every <weekday>" phrases in the description (explicit language).
2. A single weekday named in the title ("Mussels Monday", "Taco Tuesdays").
3. The concrete ``start_date`` weekday, when the payload's single-day index

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, timedelta

WEEKDAY_NAME_TO_INDEX = {
    "monday": 0,
    "tuesday": 1,
    "wednesday": 2,
    "thursday": 3,
    "friday": 4,
    "saturday": 5,
    "sunday": 6,
}

EVERY_WEEKDAY_RE = re.compile(
    r"\bevery\s+(monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|friday|saturday|sunday)s?\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

_TITLE_WEEKDAY_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|friday|saturday|sunday)s?\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


@dataclass
class AlignmentResult:
    days: str
    start_date: date
    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def weekday_from_title(title: object) -> int | None:
    """Return the weekday index named in a title, or None.

    Only trusts the title when exactly one distinct weekday is mentioned;
    "Weekend Specials Friday & Saturday" gives no single answer.
    """
    found = {
        WEEKDAY_NAME_TO_INDEX[match.group(1).lower()]
        for match in _TITLE_WEEKDAY_RE.finditer(str(title or ""))
    }
    if len(found) == 1:
        return found.pop()
    return None


def weekdays_from_description(description: object) -> list[int]:
    """Return weekday indices from "every <weekday>" phrases, in order."""
    matched: list[int] = []
    for match in EVERY_WEEKDAY_RE.finditer(str(description or "")):
        day = WEEKDAY_NAME_TO_INDEX[match.group(1).lower()]
        if day not in matched:
            matched.append(day)
    return matched


def _parse_recurrence_days(recurrence_days: str) -> tuple[list[int], list[str]]:
    days: list[int] = []
    warnings: list[str] = []
    for token in str(recurrence_days or "").split(","):
        token = token.strip()
        if not token:
            continue
        try:
            day = int(token)
        except ValueError:
            warnings.append("invalid_recurrence_day_dropped")
            continue
        if not 0 <= day <= 6:
            warnings.append("invalid_recurrence_day_dropped")
            continue
        if day not in days:
            days.append(day)
    return days, warnings


def align_weekly_recurrence(
    *,
    title: object,
    description: object,
    start_date: date,
    recurrence_days: str,
) -> AlignmentResult:
    """Reconcile a WEEKLY item's recurrence days and start date.

    Always corrects and warns; never rejects (a rejected item is invisible
    content, which is the failure mode this exists to prevent).
    """
    payload_days, warnings = _parse_recurrence_days(recurrence_days)

    description_days = weekdays_from_description(description)
    title_day = weekday_from_title(title)

    if description_days:
        days = description_days
        if payload_days and set(payload_days) != set(days):
            warnings.append("recurrence_days_realigned_from_description")
    elif title_day is not None:
        days = [title_day]

        # concrete date it extracted — trust the date over the index, since
        # wrong-convention indices are the common failure.
        days = [start_date.weekday()]
        warnings.append("recurrence_day_realigned_from_start_date")
    else:
        days = payload_days
        if days and start_date.weekday() not in days:
            warnings.append("start_weekday_not_in_recurrence_days")

    aligned_start = start_date
    if days and start_date.weekday() not in days:
        allowed = set(days)

            if candidate.weekday() in allowed:
                aligned_start = candidate
                warnings.append("start_date_realigned")
                break

    return AlignmentResult(
        days=",".join(str(day) for day in days),
        start_date=aligned_start,
        warnings=warnings,
    )

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _decode_flyer_bytes(content_base64: str) -> bytes:
    normalized = str(content_base64 or "").strip()
    if normalized.startswith("data:") and "," in normalized:
        normalized = normalized.split(",", 1)[1]
    if not normalized:
        raise ValueError("Flyer image content is required")
    try:
        return base64.b64decode(normalized, validate=True)
    except binascii.Error as exc:
        raise ValueError("Flyer image payload is not valid base64") from exc


def _normalize_flyer_content_type(*, content_type: str, original_filename: str) -> str:
    normalized = str(content_type or "").strip().lower()
    if not normalized:
        guessed, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(original_filename or "")
        normalized = str(guessed or "").lower()
    if not normalized:
        normalized = "image/png"
    if normalized not in settings.ALLOWED_IMAGE_TYPES:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported flyer image type: {normalized}")
    return normalized


def _flyer_extension(*, content_type: str, original_filename: str) -> str:
    extension = str(original_filename or "").strip()
    extension = extension.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in extension else ""
    if extension:
        return f".{extension}"
    guessed = mimetypes.guess_extension(content_type) or ".png"
    return ".jpg" if guessed == ".jpe" else guessed


def _store_flyer_image(
    *,
    event: RegionEvent,
    flyer_image: dict[str, Any],
) -> tuple[str, str]:
    content_bytes = _decode_flyer_bytes(str(flyer_image.get("content_base64") or ""))
    if len(content_bytes) > settings.MAX_IMAGE_SIZE:
        raise ValueError("Flyer image exceeds the maximum allowed size")

    original_filename = str(flyer_image.get("original_filename") or "")
    content_type = _normalize_flyer_content_type(
        content_type=str(flyer_image.get("content_type") or ""),
        original_filename=original_filename,
    )
    extension = _flyer_extension(
        content_type=content_type,
        original_filename=original_filename,
    )
    source_key = (
        str(getattr(getattr(event, "event_source", None), "source_key", "") or "region")
        .strip()
        .replace("/", "-")
    )
    digest = hashlib.sha256(content_bytes).hexdigest()
    file_key = f"region-events/flyers/{source_key}/{event.id}/{digest}{extension}"
    storage = storages["s3uploadEvents"]
    if not storage.exists(file_key):
        storage.save(file_key, ContentFile(content_bytes))
    return file_key, content_type


def _event_flyer_route(event: RegionEvent) -> str:
    return reverse("regions:event_flyer", kwargs={"event_id": event.id})


def _sync_uploaded_flyer(
    *,
    event: RegionEvent,
    flyer_image: dict[str, Any] | None,
    incoming_image_url: str,
) -> None:
    if flyer_image:
        try:
            file_key, content_type = _store_flyer_image(
                event=event,
                flyer_image=flyer_image,
            )
        except ValueError:
            logger.warning(
                "Skipping invalid flyer upload for region event %s",
                event.pk,
                exc_info=True,
            )
            return

        storage = storages["s3uploadEvents"]
        previous_file_key = str(getattr(event, "flyer_file_key", "") or "")
        route = _event_flyer_route(event)
        update_fields: list[str] = []

        if previous_file_key and previous_file_key != file_key:
            storage.delete(previous_file_key)
        if event.flyer_file_key != file_key:
            event.flyer_file_key = file_key
            update_fields.append("flyer_file_key")
        if event.flyer_content_type != content_type:
            event.flyer_content_type = content_type
            update_fields.append("flyer_content_type")
        if event.image_url != route:
            event.image_url = route
            update_fields.append("image_url")
        if update_fields:
            event.save(update_fields=update_fields)
        return

    if event.flyer_file_key and not incoming_image_url:
        route = _event_flyer_route(event)
        if event.image_url != route:
            event.image_url = route
            event.save(update_fields=["image_url"])


def _attachment_group_key(external_id: str) -> str | None:
    parts = [part for part in str(external_id or "").split(":") if part]
    if len(parts) < 3:
        return None
    return ":".join(parts[:3])


def _deactivate_missing_attachment_events(
    *,
    event_source: EventSource,
    incoming_external_ids: set[str],
) -> list[int]:
    if not incoming_external_ids:
        return []

    group_keys = {
        key
        for external_id in incoming_external_ids
        if (key := _attachment_group_key(external_id))
    }
    if not group_keys:
        return []

    stale_event_ids: list[int] = []
    for event in RegionEvent.objects.filter(
        event_source=event_source,
        category="FOOD",
        is_active=True,
    ).exclude(external_id=""):
        group_key = _attachment_group_key(event.external_id)
        if group_key in group_keys and event.external_id not in incoming_external_ids:
            stale_event_ids.append(event.id)

    if not stale_event_ids:
        return []

    RegionEvent.objects.filter(id__in=stale_event_ids).update(is_active=False)
    return stale_event_ids


#: Scraped DAILY/WEEKLY events without an explicit end date only render for
#: this many days past their start; reposts refresh the window.
SCRAPED_RECURRENCE_HORIZON_DAYS = 14


def _default_scraper_recurrence_horizon(
    *,
    event_source: EventSource,
    recurrence_pattern: str,
    start_date: date,
    recurrence_end_date: date | None,
) -> date | None:
    if recurrence_end_date is not None:
        return recurrence_end_date
    if event_source.source_type != "SCRAPER":
        return None
    if recurrence_pattern not in ("DAILY", "WEEKLY"):
        return None
    return start_date + timedelta(days=SCRAPED_RECURRENCE_HORIZON_DAYS)


def _validate_recurrence_window(
    *,
    start_date: date,
    recurrence_pattern: str,
    recurrence_end_date: date | None,
) -> None:
    if recurrence_pattern == "NONE":
        return

    if recurrence_end_date is None:
        return

    if recurrence_end_date < start_date:
        raise ValueError("recurrence_end_date cannot be earlier than start_date")


_MEAL_KEYWORDS_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:breakfast|brunch|lunch|dinner|all[- ]?day)\b", re.IGNORECASE
)


def _apply_existing_event_update(
    event: RegionEvent, defaults: dict[str, Any]
) -> RegionEvent:
    defaults = dict(defaults)
    new_start = defaults.get("start_datetime")
    if (
        event.recurrence_pattern == "NONE"
        and new_start is not None
        and timezone.localtime(new_start).date()
        != timezone.localtime(event.start_datetime).date()
    ):
        # A non-recurring event must never migrate to a different day via a
        # repost match — that is how per-day items collapsed into one row.
        logger.warning(
            "Refusing to move non-recurring region event %s from %s to %s",
            event.pk,
            event.start_datetime.date(),
            new_start.date(),
        )
        defaults.pop("start_datetime", None)
        defaults.pop("end_datetime", None)
    for field, value in defaults.items():
        setattr(event, field, value)
    event.save()
    queue_region_event_place_enrichment(event)
    return event


def _apply_meal_period_merge(
    event: RegionEvent, defaults: dict[str, Any]
) -> RegionEvent:
    """Merge a new meal-period event into an existing one from the same venue."""
    new_desc = str(defaults.get("description", "") or "")
    if new_desc:
        existing_lines = set(event.description.strip().splitlines())
        extra_lines = [
            line
            for line in new_desc.strip().splitlines()
            if line.strip() and line.strip() not in existing_lines
        ]
        if extra_lines:
            combined = event.description.rstrip()
            if combined:
                combined += "\n"
            combined += "\n".join(extra_lines)
            event.description = combined

    event.meal_period = None
    event.last_ingested_at = defaults.get("last_ingested_at") or timezone.now()

    new_start = defaults.get("start_datetime", event.start_datetime)
    new_end = defaults.get("end_datetime", event.end_datetime)
    event.start_datetime = min(event.start_datetime, new_start)
    # Meal merges only combine same-day cards; the end must stay on the
    # start day or repeated reposts grow the event into a permanent card.
    local_start = timezone.localtime(event.start_datetime)
    end_of_day = local_start.replace(hour=23, minute=59, second=59, microsecond=0)
    event.end_datetime = min(max(event.end_datetime, new_end), end_of_day)

    existing_name = str(event.name or "")
    new_name = str(defaults.get("name", "") or "")
    existing_has_meal = bool(_MEAL_KEYWORDS_RE.search(existing_name))
    new_has_meal = bool(_MEAL_KEYWORDS_RE.search(new_name))
    if existing_has_meal and not new_has_meal:
        event.name = new_name
    elif not existing_has_meal and new_has_meal:
        pass  # keep existing (no meal keyword)
    elif existing_has_meal and new_has_meal:
        # Both have meal keywords — strip the meal keyword from existing
        stripped = _MEAL_KEYWORDS_RE.sub("", existing_name).strip()
        stripped = re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", stripped)
        if stripped:
            event.name = stripped

    for field in ("image_url", "external_url", "address"):
        existing_val = getattr(event, field, "")
        new_val = defaults.get(field, "")
        if not existing_val and new_val:
            setattr(event, field, new_val)

    event.save()
    queue_region_event_place_enrichment(event)
    return event


class EventIngestView(APIView):
    """POST /api/region-events/ingest/

    Receives a batch of scraped events and upserts them as RegionEvent records.
    """

    authentication_classes = [SharedSecretAuthentication]
    permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated]

    def post(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        serializer = IngestRequestSerializer(data=request.data)
        serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True)
        data = serializer.validated_data

        # Look up the EventSource
        source_key: str = data["source_key"]

        system_user = get_system_calendar_user()
        created = 0

        if replace_existing_attachment_events:

                recurrence_pattern = event_data.get("recurrence_pattern") or "NONE"

                    if alignment.start_date != start_date:
                        end_date = end_date + (alignment.start_date - start_date)
                        start_date = alignment.start_date
                    if alignment.warnings:

def _decode_flyer_bytes(content_base64: str) -> bytes:
    normalized = str(content_base64 or "").strip()
    if normalized.startswith("data:") and "," in normalized:
        normalized = normalized.split(",", 1)[1]
    if not normalized:
        raise ValueError("Flyer image content is required")
    try:
        return base64.b64decode(normalized, validate=True)
    except binascii.Error as exc:
        raise ValueError("Flyer image payload is not valid base64") from exc


def _normalize_flyer_content_type(*, content_type: str, original_filename: str) -> str:
    normalized = str(content_type or "").strip().lower()
    if not normalized:
        guessed, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(original_filename or "")
        normalized = str(guessed or "").lower()
    if not normalized:
        normalized = "image/png"
    if normalized not in settings.ALLOWED_IMAGE_TYPES:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported flyer image type: {normalized}")
    return normalized


def _flyer_extension(*, content_type: str, original_filename: str) -> str:
    extension = str(original_filename or "").strip()
    extension = extension.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in extension else ""
    if extension:
        return f".{extension}"
    guessed = mimetypes.guess_extension(content_type) or ".png"
    return ".jpg" if guessed == ".jpe" else guessed


def _store_flyer_image(
    *,
    event: RegionEvent,
    flyer_image: dict[str, Any],
) -> tuple[str, str]:
    content_bytes = _decode_flyer_bytes(str(flyer_image.get("content_base64") or ""))
    if len(content_bytes) > settings.MAX_IMAGE_SIZE:
        raise ValueError("Flyer image exceeds the maximum allowed size")

    original_filename = str(flyer_image.get("original_filename") or "")
    content_type = _normalize_flyer_content_type(
        content_type=str(flyer_image.get("content_type") or ""),
        original_filename=original_filename,
    )
    extension = _flyer_extension(
        content_type=content_type,
        original_filename=original_filename,
    )
    source_key = (
        str(getattr(getattr(event, "event_source", None), "source_key", "") or "region")
        .strip()
        .replace("/", "-")
    )
    digest = hashlib.sha256(content_bytes).hexdigest()
    file_key = f"region-events/flyers/{source_key}/{event.id}/{digest}{extension}"
    storage = storages["s3uploadEvents"]
    if not storage.exists(file_key):
        storage.save(file_key, ContentFile(content_bytes))
    return file_key, content_type


def _event_flyer_route(event: RegionEvent) -> str:
    return reverse("regions:event_flyer", kwargs={"event_id": event.id})


def _sync_uploaded_flyer(
    *,
    event: RegionEvent,
    flyer_image: dict[str, Any] | None,
    incoming_image_url: str,
) -> None:
    if flyer_image:
        try:
            file_key, content_type = _store_flyer_image(
                event=event,
                flyer_image=flyer_image,
            )
        except ValueError:
            logger.warning(
                "Skipping invalid flyer upload for region event %s",
                event.pk,
                exc_info=True,
            )
            return

        storage = storages["s3uploadEvents"]
        previous_file_key = str(getattr(event, "flyer_file_key", "") or "")
        route = _event_flyer_route(event)
        update_fields: list[str] = []

        if previous_file_key and previous_file_key != file_key:
            storage.delete(previous_file_key)
        if event.flyer_file_key != file_key:
            event.flyer_file_key = file_key
            update_fields.append("flyer_file_key")
        if event.flyer_content_type != content_type:
            event.flyer_content_type = content_type
            update_fields.append("flyer_content_type")
        if event.image_url != route:
            event.image_url = route
            update_fields.append("image_url")
        if update_fields:
            event.save(update_fields=update_fields)
        return

    if event.flyer_file_key and not incoming_image_url:
        route = _event_flyer_route(event)
        if event.image_url != route:
            event.image_url = route
            event.save(update_fields=["image_url"])


def _attachment_group_key(external_id: str) -> str | None:
    parts = [part for part in str(external_id or "").split(":") if part]
    if len(parts) < 3:
        return None
    return ":".join(parts[:3])


def _deactivate_missing_attachment_events(
    *,
    event_source: EventSource,
    incoming_external_ids: set[str],
) -> list[int]:
    if not incoming_external_ids:
        return []

    group_keys = {
        key
        for external_id in incoming_external_ids
        if (key := _attachment_group_key(external_id))
    }
    if not group_keys:
        return []

    stale_event_ids: list[int] = []
    for event in RegionEvent.objects.filter(
        event_source=event_source,
        category="FOOD",
        is_active=True,
    ).exclude(external_id=""):
        group_key = _attachment_group_key(event.external_id)
        if group_key in group_keys and event.external_id not in incoming_external_ids:
            stale_event_ids.append(event.id)

    if not stale_event_ids:
        return []

    RegionEvent.objects.filter(id__in=stale_event_ids).update(is_active=False)
    return stale_event_ids


#: Scraped DAILY/WEEKLY events without an explicit end date only render for
#: this many days past their start; reposts refresh the window.
SCRAPED_RECURRENCE_HORIZON_DAYS = 14


def _default_scraper_recurrence_horizon(
    *,
    event_source: EventSource,
    recurrence_pattern: str,
    start_date: date,
    recurrence_end_date: date | None,
) -> date | None:
    if recurrence_end_date is not None:
        return recurrence_end_date
    if event_source.source_type != "SCRAPER":
        return None
    if recurrence_pattern not in ("DAILY", "WEEKLY"):
        return None
    return start_date + timedelta(days=SCRAPED_RECURRENCE_HORIZON_DAYS)


def _validate_recurrence_window(
    *,
    start_date: date,
    recurrence_pattern: str,
    recurrence_end_date: date | None,
) -> None:
    if recurrence_pattern == "NONE":
        return

    if recurrence_end_date is None:
        return

    if recurrence_end_date < start_date:
        raise ValueError("recurrence_end_date cannot be earlier than start_date")


_MEAL_KEYWORDS_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:breakfast|brunch|lunch|dinner|all[- ]?day)\b", re.IGNORECASE
)


def _apply_existing_event_update(
    event: RegionEvent, defaults: dict[str, Any]
) -> RegionEvent:
    defaults = dict(defaults)
    new_start = defaults.get("start_datetime")
    if (
        event.recurrence_pattern == "NONE"
        and new_start is not None
        and timezone.localtime(new_start).date()
        != timezone.localtime(event.start_datetime).date()
    ):
        # A non-recurring event must never migrate to a different day via a
        # repost match — that is how per-day items collapsed into one row.
        logger.warning(
            "Refusing to move non-recurring region event %s from %s to %s",
            event.pk,
            event.start_datetime.date(),
            new_start.date(),
        )
        defaults.pop("start_datetime", None)
        defaults.pop("end_datetime", None)
    for field, value in defaults.items():
        setattr(event, field, value)
    event.save()
    queue_region_event_place_enrichment(event)
    return event


def _apply_meal_period_merge(
    event: RegionEvent, defaults: dict[str, Any]
) -> RegionEvent:
    """Merge a new meal-period event into an existing one from the same venue."""
    new_desc = str(defaults.get("description", "") or "")
    if new_desc:
        existing_lines = set(event.description.strip().splitlines())
        extra_lines = [
            line
            for line in new_desc.strip().splitlines()
            if line.strip() and line.strip() not in existing_lines
        ]
        if extra_lines:
            combined = event.description.rstrip()
            if combined:
                combined += "\n"
            combined += "\n".join(extra_lines)
            event.description = combined

    event.meal_period = None
    event.last_ingested_at = defaults.get("last_ingested_at") or timezone.now()

    new_start = defaults.get("start_datetime", event.start_datetime)
    new_end = defaults.get("end_datetime", event.end_datetime)
    event.start_datetime = min(event.start_datetime, new_start)
    # Meal merges only combine same-day cards; the end must stay on the
    # start day or repeated reposts grow the event into a permanent card.
    local_start = timezone.localtime(event.start_datetime)
    end_of_day = local_start.replace(hour=23, minute=59, second=59, microsecond=0)
    event.end_datetime = min(max(event.end_datetime, new_end), end_of_day)

    existing_name = str(event.name or "")
    new_name = str(defaults.get("name", "") or "")
    existing_has_meal = bool(_MEAL_KEYWORDS_RE.search(existing_name))
    new_has_meal = bool(_MEAL_KEYWORDS_RE.search(new_name))
    if existing_has_meal and not new_has_meal:
        event.name = new_name
    elif not existing_has_meal and new_has_meal:
        pass  # keep existing (no meal keyword)
    elif existing_has_meal and new_has_meal:
        # Both have meal keywords — strip the meal keyword from existing
        stripped = _MEAL_KEYWORDS_RE.sub("", existing_name).strip()
        stripped = re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", stripped)
        if stripped:
            event.name = stripped

    for field in ("image_url", "external_url", "address"):
        existing_val = getattr(event, field, "")
        new_val = defaults.get(field, "")
        if not existing_val and new_val:
            setattr(event, field, new_val)

    event.save()
    queue_region_event_place_enrichment(event)
    return event

        errors = 0

"""Detection and repair of ingest damage on RegionEvent rows.

Backs the ``repair_region_event_ingest`` management command and the
read-only sections of ``audit_region_event_ingest``. Each detector returns
:class:`RepairFinding` records describing the issue and the proposed
change; ``apply`` performs the change.

Issue classes (from REGION_INGEST_AUDIT_2026-06.md):
- ``unbounded_recurrence``: DAILY/WEEKLY scraped events with no
  recurrence_end_date render until Dec 31 (zombie cards).
- ``overspanned_food``: non-recurring FOOD events spanning many days show a
  stale menu on every spanned day.
- ``weekday_mismatch``: WEEKLY rows whose recurrence_days disagree with the
  weekday named in the title / the start date (Sunday=0 payloads).
- ``duplicate_venue_day``: two active events from the same source rendering
  for the same venue on the same day.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, timedelta
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from django.utils import timezone

from trips.services.dedup_service import (
    SAME_SOURCE_NAME_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD,
    names_match,
    normalize_name,
)
from trips.services.recurrence_alignment import (
    AlignmentResult,
    align_weekly_recurrence,
    weekday_from_title,
)

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from datetime import datetime

    from django.db.models import QuerySet

    from trips.models import RegionEvent

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: How far past the last confirmation a scraped recurrence may keep rendering.
SCRAPED_RECURRENCE_HORIZON_DAYS = 14

#: Maximum plausible span for a non-recurring FOOD special.
MAX_FOOD_SPAN_DAYS = 7

#: How far ahead to expand occurrences when looking for venue-day duplicates.
DUPLICATE_HORIZON_DAYS = 14


@dataclass
class RepairFinding:
    event: RegionEvent
    issue_class: str
    description: str
    apply: Callable[[], None]


def _active_source_events(source_key: str) -> QuerySet[RegionEvent]:
    from trips.models import RegionEvent

    return RegionEvent.objects.filter(
        event_source__source_key=source_key,
        is_active=True,
    ).select_related("event_source")


def find_unbounded_scraped_recurrences(source_key: str) -> list[RepairFinding]:
    """DAILY/WEEKLY scraped events with no recurrence end date."""
    findings: list[RepairFinding] = []
    events = _active_source_events(source_key).filter(
        recurrence_pattern__in=["DAILY", "WEEKLY"],
        recurrence_end_date__isnull=True,
        event_source__source_type="SCRAPER",
    )
    for event in events:
        anchor = (
            timezone.localtime(event.last_ingested_at).date()
            if event.last_ingested_at
            else timezone.localtime(event.start_datetime).date()
        )
        proposed_end = anchor + timedelta(days=SCRAPED_RECURRENCE_HORIZON_DAYS)

        def apply(
            event: RegionEvent = event, proposed_end: date = proposed_end
        ) -> None:
            event.recurrence_end_date = proposed_end
            event.save(update_fields=["recurrence_end_date"])

        findings.append(
            RepairFinding(
                event=event,
                issue_class="unbounded_recurrence",
                description=(
                    f"{event.recurrence_pattern} with no end date; "
                    f"set recurrence_end_date={proposed_end.isoformat()}"
                ),
                apply=apply,
            )
        )
    return findings


def find_overspanned_food(
    source_key: str, *, max_days: int = MAX_FOOD_SPAN_DAYS
) -> list[RepairFinding]:
    """Non-recurring FOOD events spanning more than ``max_days`` days."""
    findings: list[RepairFinding] = []
    events = _active_source_events(source_key).filter(
        category="FOOD",
        recurrence_pattern="NONE",
    )
    for event in events:
        local_start = timezone.localtime(event.start_datetime)
        local_end = timezone.localtime(event.end_datetime)
        span_days = (local_end.date() - local_start.date()).days
        if span_days <= max_days:
            continue
        proposed_end = local_start.replace(hour=23, minute=59, second=59, microsecond=0)

        def apply(
            event: RegionEvent = event, proposed_end: datetime = proposed_end
        ) -> None:
            event.end_datetime = proposed_end
            event.save(update_fields=["end_datetime"])

        findings.append(
            RepairFinding(
                event=event,
                issue_class="overspanned_food",
                description=(
                    f"NONE FOOD event spans {span_days} days "
                    f"({local_start.date()} -> {local_end.date()}); "
                    f"truncate end to {proposed_end.date().isoformat()}"
                ),
                apply=apply,
            )
        )
    return findings


def find_weekday_mismatched_weekly(source_key: str) -> list[RepairFinding]:
    """WEEKLY single-day rows whose day index contradicts title/start date."""
    findings: list[RepairFinding] = []
    events = _active_source_events(source_key).filter(recurrence_pattern="WEEKLY")
    for event in events:
        days = [
            int(token)
            for token in str(event.recurrence_days or "").split(",")
            if token.strip().lstrip("-").isdigit()
        ]
        if len(days) != 1:
            continue
        local_start_date = timezone.localtime(event.start_datetime).date()
        title_day = weekday_from_title(event.name)
        if days[0] == local_start_date.weekday():
            continue
        if title_day is not None and days[0] == title_day:
            continue

        alignment = align_weekly_recurrence(
            title=event.name,
            description=event.description,
            start_date=local_start_date,
            recurrence_days=event.recurrence_days,
        )
        if alignment.days == event.recurrence_days:
            continue

        def apply(
            event: RegionEvent = event, alignment: AlignmentResult = alignment
        ) -> None:
            event.recurrence_days = alignment.days
            update_fields = ["recurrence_days"]
            local_start = timezone.localtime(event.start_datetime)
            if alignment.start_date != local_start.date():
                delta = alignment.start_date - local_start.date()
                event.start_datetime = event.start_datetime + delta
                event.end_datetime = event.end_datetime + delta
                update_fields += ["start_datetime", "end_datetime"]
            event.save(update_fields=update_fields)

        findings.append(
            RepairFinding(
                event=event,
                issue_class="weekday_mismatch",
                description=(
                    f"WEEKLY days={event.recurrence_days!r} contradicts "
                    f"start weekday {local_start_date.weekday()} "
                    f"and title; realign to days={alignment.days!r}"
                ),
                apply=apply,
            )
        )
    return findings


def find_duplicate_venue_day(
    source_key: str, *, horizon_days: int = DUPLICATE_HORIZON_DAYS
) -> list[RepairFinding]:
    """Pairs of same-source events rendering for the same venue on a day.

    Keeps the older row (lower pk) and proposes deactivating the newer one.
    """
    today = timezone.localdate()
    horizon_end = today + timedelta(days=horizon_days)

    events = list(
        _active_source_events(source_key).filter(category="FOOD").exclude(location="")
    )

    by_venue_day: dict[tuple[str, date], list[RegionEvent]] = {}
    for event in events:
        venue = normalize_name(event.location)
        if not venue:
            continue
        for occurrence_date in event._iter_occurrence_dates(today, horizon_end):
            by_venue_day.setdefault((venue, occurrence_date), []).append(event)

    flagged: set[int] = set()
    findings: list[RepairFinding] = []
    for (venue, occurrence_date), group in sorted(
        by_venue_day.items(), key=lambda item: (item[0][1], item[0][0])
    ):
        if len(group) < 2:
            continue
        group = sorted(set(group), key=lambda event: event.pk)
        keep = group[0]
        for candidate in group[1:]:
            if candidate.pk in flagged:
                continue
            if (
                names_match(keep.name, candidate.name)
                < SAME_SOURCE_NAME_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD
            ):
                continue
            flagged.add(candidate.pk)

            def apply(event: RegionEvent = candidate) -> None:
                event.is_active = False
                event.save(update_fields=["is_active"])

            findings.append(
                RepairFinding(
                    event=candidate,
                    issue_class="duplicate_venue_day",
                    description=(
                        f"Duplicates event {keep.pk} ('{keep.name}') for venue "
                        f"'{venue}' on {occurrence_date.isoformat()}; deactivate"
                    ),
                    apply=apply,
                )
            )
    return findings


ISSUE_DETECTORS: dict[str, Callable[[str], list[RepairFinding]]] = {
    "unbounded_recurrence": find_unbounded_scraped_recurrences,
    "overspanned_food": find_overspanned_food,
    "weekday_mismatch": find_weekday_mismatched_weekly,
    "duplicate_venue_day": find_duplicate_venue_day,
}


def find_all_issues(source_key: str, *, only: str | None = None) -> list[RepairFinding]:
    findings: list[RepairFinding] = []
    for issue_class, detector in ISSUE_DETECTORS.items():
        if only and issue_class != only:
            continue
        findings.extend(detector(source_key))
    return findings

def find_all_issues(source_key: str, *, only: str | None = None) -> list[RepairFinding]:

content.text:
Yes — on prod after `git pull` (in order):

**1. Migrate** (new `last_ingested_at` column, migration `trips/0033`):
```bash
python3 manage.py migrate trips
```
Then restart the app per your usual deploy step.

**2. Prod data cleanup** (the audit's item 5 — code fixes stop *new* damage, but zombies 153/339, Henry's 738, and Sunday-convention rows already in the DB need repair):
```bash
# dry-run first — confirm ids 153, 339, 738 and weekday-mismatch rows show up
python3 manage.py repair_region_event_ingest --source-key <obx-source-key>

# then apply
python3 manage.py repair_region_event_ingest --source-key <obx-source-key> --apply

# confirm detections zeroed
python3 manage.py audit_region_event_ingest --source-key <obx-source-key>
```
(Source key = the `EventSource.source_key` for the OBX specials scraper — likely `outer-banks-specials`; the dry-run errors clearly if wrong.)

**3. Spot-check** `https://app.clancal.com/explore/outer-banks-nc/specials/` — Jolly Roger Happy Hour and Snow Birds should be gone from today's page, single Henry's card.

Order matters: migrate before repair (the repair command reads `last_ingested_at`). All cleanup is dry-run-default and `--apply` runs in one transaction, so nothing mutates until you've eyeballed the findings list.

Nothing else backend-side. The scraper steps (deploy to listener host, add `specials_feed_url` to `outer_banks.yml`, reconcile cron, supervised replay for the external_id cutover) are separate and can come after — backend is safe to deploy alone; it just defends harder against the old payload shapes until the scraper catches up.

content.text:
You're right — my instruction was wrong. The migration is fully in the codebase and your deploy already applies it: `docker-entrypoint.sh:8` runs `python manage.py migrate --no-input` on every container start. Deploy normally; `trips/0033` applies itself. No manual migrate, no drift risk.

So the actual post-deploy steps reduce to one thing:

**The one-time data repair** (this stays manual on purpose — it deactivates/rewrites existing prod rows, and you want to eyeball the findings before mutating):
```bash
python3 manage.py repair_region_event_ingest --source-key <obx-source-key>            # dry-run, review
python3 manage.py repair_region_event_ingest --source-key <obx-source-key> --apply   # fix
python3 manage.py audit_region_event_ingest --source-key <obx-source-key>            # confirm zeroed
```

That's cleanup of *damage already in the database* (zombies 153/339, Henry's 738 span, Sunday-convention rows) — the deployed code prevents new damage but doesn't rewrite history on its own. After this one run there's nothing recurring on the backend side; the nightly reconcile job (scraper repo) is what watches for regressions going forward.
